0.name: Generative and Sequential Recommendation
0.one_line: These papers build LLM-based recommender systems that generate semantic item IDs, model user histories and preferences, and suggest queries in e-commerce search.

1.name: Self-Improving Reasoning and Self-Correction
1.one_line: These papers improve model reasoning through self-evolution, reinforcement learning with guided exploration, latent reasoning and activation steering, alongside some work on calibration and abstention.

2.name: Graph RAG and Multi-Hop QA
2.one_line: These papers answer multi-hop questions by retrieving evidence over knowledge graphs, hypergraphs and document graphs, often with agentic or iterative retrieval.

3.name: Psycholinguistics and Linguistic Knowledge Probing
3.one_line: These papers compare language models with human sentence processing and test their syntactic, lexical and typological knowledge, with a mix of morphology, parsing and corpus work.

4.name: Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
4.one_line: These papers attack and defend tool-using agents against indirect prompt injection and build red-teaming methods and benchmarks for agent security.

5.name: Agent Skill Libraries and Skill Evolution
5.one_line: These papers let agents distill, retrieve, revise and evolve reusable procedural skills from execution traces, a topic that is new in 2026.

6.name: Emotion Recognition and Affective Analysis
6.one_line: These papers recognize, explain and control emotion, sentiment and stance in text and conversation, and probe how models represent affect internally.

7.name: Document Information Extraction and Enterprise QA
7.one_line: These papers extract structured information from corporate, financial and office documents and benchmark question answering over enterprise document collections, with some legal and biomedical extraction mixed in.

8.name: Dense Retrieval and LLM Reranking
8.one_line: These papers train dense and generative retrievers and LLM rerankers, with a focus on reasoning-intensive and efficient text retrieval.

9.name: Spatial Reasoning and 3D Visual Grounding
9.one_line: These papers evaluate and improve the spatial reasoning of vision-language models, including perspective taking, 3D visual grounding, geolocalization and remote sensing.

10.name: Long and Streaming Video QA
10.one_line: These papers help video language models answer questions about long and streaming videos through frame selection, evidence search and hierarchical multimodal memory.

11.name: Machine Unlearning in Language Models
11.one_line: These papers remove targeted knowledge from text and multimodal models while preserving utility, and test how robust the forgetting is to relearning and recovery attacks.

12.name: Confidence Calibration and Knowledge Boundaries
12.one_line: These papers study whether models know what they know, covering verbal confidence calibration, belief stability, honesty, overconfidence and hallucination mechanisms.

13.name: Benchmark Construction and Evaluation Reliability
13.one_line: These papers build new evaluation benchmarks across domains and languages and question benchmark validity through contamination detection, compression and diagnostic analysis.

14.name: Cross-Lingual Transfer and Multilingual Representations
14.one_line: These papers measure and close the gap between English and other languages through cross-lingual alignment, representation analysis, multilingual judges and multilingual training data.

15.name: Automated Peer Review and Essay Scoring
15.one_line: These papers generate, verify and audit scientific peer reviews with language models, alongside work on multi-trait essay scoring and deep research report evaluation.

16.name: KV Cache Compression and Eviction
16.one_line: These papers shrink the key-value cache for long-context inference through token eviction, quantization, low-rank approximation and adaptive per-layer budgets.

17.name: Clarifying Questions and Information-Seeking QA
17.one_line: These papers study how assistants ask clarifying questions, answer information-seeking and misconception-laden queries, and evaluate open QA, mixed with assorted conversation analytics and pragmatics work.

18.name: Authorship Style and Creative Writing
18.one_line: These papers analyze and transfer writing style for authorship attribution and personalized generation, and measure diversity and creativity in machine-written stories and poetry.

19.name: Role-Playing Agents and Emotional Support Dialogue
19.one_line: These papers train and evaluate role-playing characters, counseling and emotional support agents, and user simulators for multi-turn dialogue, with some general conversational assistant work.

20.name: Multimodal and Text-to-Image Safety
20.one_line: These papers benchmark and defend multimodal and text-to-image models against unsafe generation, jailbreaks and culturally specific risks, using safety unlearning, detoxification and guard models.

21.name: Diffusion Language Models and Parallel Decoding
21.one_line: These papers build, scale and speed up masked and continuous diffusion language models, with new remasking, parallel decoding, length control and distillation strategies.

22.name: Attention, State-Space and Hybrid Architectures
22.one_line: These papers analyze and redesign sequence model architectures such as Transformers, linear attention, Mamba-style state-space models and hybrids, covering positional encoding, attention sinks and layer representations.

23.name: LLM-as-a-Judge Bias and Reliability
23.one_line: These papers test how reliable LLM judges are, exposing position, self-preference and rubric biases and proposing debiasing, calibration and measurement-theory fixes, alongside a few fairness auditing studies.

24.name: Long-Horizon Agents and World Models
24.one_line: These papers train language agents for long-horizon interactive tasks using learned world models, experience reuse, context management and self-evolving policies in environments like ALFWorld and WebShop.

25.name: Vision-Language Model Failures and Robustness
25.one_line: These papers diagnose where vision-language models fail, including language priors overriding perception, framing effects, false premises, miscalibrated confidence and unfaithful visual grounding.

26.name: Cultural Knowledge and Cultural Alignment
26.one_line: These papers benchmark and steer how language models understand and adapt to cultural norms, values and region-specific knowledge across many languages and societies.

27.name: Mathematical Reasoning and Formal Theorem Proving
27.one_line: These papers improve and evaluate mathematical problem solving through verifiers, process reward models, distractor robustness, autoformalization and formal proof benchmarks.

28.name: Medical Question Answering and Medical VQA
28.one_line: These papers build and evaluate medical reasoning models for question answering and medical visual question answering, using reinforcement learning, multilingual medical data and evidence-grounded training.

29.name: Optimization Modeling and Evolutionary Algorithm Discovery
29.one_line: These papers use language models to formulate operations research and optimization problems and to evolve algorithms, code and designs through search-based self-improvement loops.

30.name: Video Benchmarks and Text-to-Video Generation
30.one_line: These papers benchmark and improve video-language models on temporal reasoning, captioning, cross-video question answering and text-to-video generation quality.

31.name: Speech Language Models and Voice Agents
31.one_line: These papers evaluate and build speech language models, spoken dialogue systems and voice agents, covering speech recognition, speech translation, TTS evaluation and multilingual speech benchmarks.

32.name: AI-Generated Text Detection
32.one_line: These papers detect and attribute machine-generated text with zero-shot statistics, probes and trained detectors, and audit detector shortcuts, robustness and cross-lingual performance.

33.name: Model Pruning and Sparsity
33.one_line: These papers compress language models through structured pruning, quantization and distillation and measure real inference speedups, while the cluster also mixes in assorted training, data selection and representation studies.

34.name: Chemistry, Molecules and Drug Discovery
34.one_line: These papers apply language models and agents to molecular property prediction, molecular optimization, retrosynthesis, structure elucidation, protein design and drug discovery.

35.name: Long-Term Memory for Agents
35.one_line: These papers design and benchmark long-term memory systems for conversational and personalized agents, covering memory extraction, consolidation, hierarchical organization and retrieval.

36.name: Theory of Mind and Social Intelligence
36.one_line: These papers benchmark theory-of-mind and social reasoning in text and multimodal models, from multi-party meetings and body language to deception and social deduction games.

37.name: Clinical Reasoning and EHR Benchmarks
37.one_line: These papers evaluate and train models for clinical decision making over electronic health records, multi-turn medical consultations and diagnosis, with a focus on evidence use and rubric-based assessment.

38.name: Chart and Visual Document Reasoning
38.one_line: These papers benchmark and improve vision-language models on charts, diagrams, scientific figures and text-rich images, with a few studies on art, manga and specialized layouts.

39.name: Direct Preference Optimization and Personalized Alignment
39.one_line: These papers refine preference alignment with token-weighted and noise-robust DPO variants, preference data selection, multi-objective steering and personalized or pluralistic alignment.

40.name: Vision-Language Hallucination Mitigation
40.one_line: These papers detect and reduce hallucinations, mostly object hallucinations in vision-language models, using attention-head interventions, activation steering, decoding fixes and new benchmarks.

41.name: Speech Synthesis, Recognition and Audio Tokenizers
41.one_line: These papers build and adapt speech and audio models for text-to-speech, speech recognition, streaming speech translation and audio tokenization.

42.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Evidence Grounding
42.one_line: These papers improve how RAG systems select, trust and cite retrieved evidence, covering knowledge conflicts, poisoning robustness, attribution and RAG evaluation.

43.name: Dialects, Scripts and Underrepresented Languages
43.one_line: These papers study dialects, writing systems and romanized or cross-script text in Arabic, Indic, African and other low-resource languages, alongside a mix of other language-specific resources and benchmarks.

44.name: Domain Adaptation and Continual Pre-Training
44.one_line: These papers adapt pretrained models to new domains through supervised fine-tuning, continual pre-training and parameter-efficient methods while limiting catastrophic forgetting of general skills.

45.name: Compliance Checking and Auditing Agents
45.one_line: These papers build agentic systems and benchmarks for claim verification, regulatory and advertising compliance checking, fraud detection and evidence-grounded auditing in applied domains.

46.name: Machine Translation Quality Evaluation
46.one_line: These papers evaluate machine translation with LLM judges, error span detection, document context and human studies, including literary and culturally loaded translation.

47.name: Tool Use and Function Calling Agents
47.one_line: These papers train and evaluate agents that select, retrieve and call external tools and APIs, with synthetic tool-use data, policy optimization and large tool ecosystems.

48.name: Text Watermarking and Model Fingerprinting
48.one_line: These papers embed and detect watermarks in generated text and fingerprint models for copyright protection, balancing detectability, robustness to edits and text quality.

49.name: Proactive Agents and Implicit User Intent
49.one_line: These papers benchmark and train agents that infer implicit user intent, elicit preferences and personalize multi-turn help in shopping, travel planning and assistant settings.

50.name: Cognitive Bias, Sycophancy and Moral Judgment
50.one_line: These papers probe language models with methods from psychology and social science, measuring sycophancy, cognitive and social biases, persuasion, moral reasoning and human-model behavioral gaps.

51.name: Omni-Modal Models and Modality Robustness
51.one_line: These papers examine modality bias, uncertainty and robustness in omni-modal and multimodal models, mixed with assorted work on incomplete multimodal learning, emotion recognition and multimodal data pipelines.

52.name: GUI Agent Grounding and RL Training
52.one_line: These papers build benchmarks, GUI grounding methods, world models and reinforcement learning recipes for agents that operate desktop, mobile and browser interfaces.

53.name: Efficient and Latent Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
53.one_line: These papers cut overthinking in reasoning models through chain-of-thought compression, adaptive token budgets, early stopping, parallel thinking and latent or implicit reasoning.

54.name: Deep Research and Search Agents
54.one_line: These papers train and evaluate agents that run long-horizon web search for deep research, using reinforcement learning, synthetic search environments and trajectory synthesis.

55.name: Human and LLM Data Annotation
55.one_line: These papers study how humans and LLMs annotate data, covering annotator disagreement and label variation, noisy labels, annotation guidelines and cost-aware human-AI labeling pipelines.

56.name: RLVR and On-Policy Distillation
56.one_line: These papers refine reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards and on-policy distillation for reasoning, tackling credit assignment, entropy collapse, advantage estimation and label-free rewards.

57.name: Table Reasoning and Table Question Answering
57.one_line: These papers answer questions and reason over tables, including multi-table retrieval, SQL-guided decomposition, table graphs and multimodal table images.

58.name: Coding Agents for Software Engineering
58.one_line: These papers benchmark and train coding agents on repository-level tasks such as issue localization, program repair, code retrieval and refactoring.

59.name: User Simulators and Human Behavior Simulation
59.one_line: These papers use language models to simulate users, personas and social behavior for evaluating agents and studying surveys and online discourse, and test how faithful these simulations are.

60.name: Mixture-of-Experts Routing and Fine-Tuning
60.one_line: These papers improve how MoE models route tokens to experts, prune or reduce experts at test time, and fine-tune MoE models without breaking their routing structure.

61.name: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness and Reasoning Diagnostics
61.one_line: These papers analyze why chain-of-thought reasoning fails, whether reasoning traces are faithful, and how to benchmark logical and causal reasoning, alongside work on overthinking and test-time compute.

62.name: Visually Grounded Multimodal Reasoning with RL
62.one_line: These papers train vision-language models to reason while keeping attention on visual evidence, using reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, latent visual thinking and visual self-correction.

63.name: Speculative Decoding and Inference Acceleration
63.one_line: These papers speed up language model inference with draft models, draft trees, retrieval-based drafting and smarter verification, plus related work on efficient sampling.

64.name: Document-Level and Low-Resource Translation
64.one_line: These papers study how language models translate, build translation benchmarks and metrics, and improve document-level and low-resource machine translation with reasoning and reinforcement learning.

65.name: Multi-Agent Debate and Argumentation
65.one_line: These papers improve multi-agent debate for reasoning through better moderation, memory and aggregation, and study persuasion, counterargument generation and competitive debating.

66.name: Event Extraction and Time-Series Grounding
66.one_line: These papers extract events, arguments and timelines from documents and connect language with time-series data for event detection, forecasting and temporal explanation.

67.name: Radiology Report Generation
67.one_line: These papers generate and evaluate radiology reports from chest X-rays and CT scans with medical vision-language models that stay grounded in images and clinical findings.

68.name: Social Bias, Stereotypes and Debiasing
68.one_line: These papers measure and trace gender, racial and occupational stereotypes inside language models and debias them, with a share of work on steering vectors and refusal directions more generally.

69.name: Legal Reasoning and Judgment Prediction
69.one_line: These papers build benchmarks, retrieval systems and reasoning models for legal judgment prediction, legal case retrieval and legal question answering across jurisdictions.

70.name: Text-to-SQL and Database Querying
70.one_line: These papers translate natural language into SQL with schema linking, chain-of-thought training, reinforcement learning and candidate selection, and build more realistic text-to-SQL benchmarks.

71.name: Scientific Discovery, Writing and Citations
71.one_line: These papers use language models for research ideation, scientific discovery, paper writing and verification, and study how AI changes citation behavior and scientific prose.

72.name: Entity Linking, Relation Extraction and Taxonomies
72.one_line: These papers link entities to knowledge bases, extract relations and named entities, and induce taxonomies, mixed with assorted work on topic modeling, embedding geometry and intent discovery.

73.name: Agent Benchmarks and Failure Diagnosis
73.one_line: These papers benchmark and debug LLM agents on real-world planning, enterprise workflows and MCP tool use, and diagnose failures from agent execution trajectories.

74.name: Safety Alignment and Over-Refusal
74.one_line: These papers study how safety alignment and refusal work inside models, defend against jailbreaks and over-refusal, preserve safety during fine-tuning and benchmark content moderation.

75.name: Synthetic Data Generation and Data Curation
75.one_line: These papers generate, select and audit synthetic training data for instruction tuning, pretraining and low-resource tasks, and design data mixtures and recipes for model adaptation.

76.name: Webpage, SVG and Text-to-Image Generation
76.one_line: These papers generate and evaluate visual artifacts such as webpages, SVG graphics, diagrams, slides and charts from code, and benchmark text-to-image generation and editing.

77.name: Multimodal RAG and Visual Document Retrieval
77.one_line: These papers retrieve images and visually rich documents with multimodal embeddings and late interaction, and use them in multimodal retrieval-augmented generation for long-document question answering.

78.name: MoE Compression and Efficient Training
78.one_line: These papers compress, merge and quantize mixture-of-experts models and make MoE training and fine-tuning more efficient, alongside some work on the Muon optimizer and parallelism.

79.name: GUI Agent Benchmarks and Simulators
79.one_line: These papers build benchmarks, simulators and frameworks for agents that operate mobile apps, desktops and web interfaces, testing long-horizon tasks, ambiguity handling and safety.

80.name: Code Generation, Testing and Repair
80.one_line: These papers train and evaluate code models with unit-test generation, execution feedback, reward models and debugging to make generated code functionally correct.

81.name: Knowledge Editing and Lifelong Model Editing
81.one_line: These papers update or reverse specific facts and rules inside model parameters, covering batch, multi-hop, temporal and lifelong editing while preserving locality.

82.name: AI Tutoring and Educational Dialogue
82.one_line: These papers build and evaluate adaptive tutoring agents, student simulators and teacher-student dialogue corpora, alongside a smaller group of knowledge distillation papers pulled in by teacher-student wording.

83.name: Agentic RL and Reward Design
83.one_line: These papers improve reinforcement learning for long-horizon agents and reasoning with better credit assignment, rubric and process rewards, rollout budgeting and defenses against reward hacking.

84.name: Personalization and Personality Alignment
84.one_line: These papers adapt model responses to individual users through user profiles, memory selection, preference tracing, persona steering and personality or value alignment.

85.name: Visual Token Pruning for Efficient VLMs
85.one_line: These papers cut inference cost in vision-language models by pruning, compressing or condensing visual tokens, with some papers on other efficiency and high-resolution adaptation methods for VLMs.

86.name: Multi-Agent Collaboration and Communication
86.one_line: These papers design and debug multi-agent LLM systems, covering role and topology adaptation, message pruning, latent communication, failure attribution and robustness to faulty agents.

87.name: Fact-Checking and Factuality Evaluation
87.one_line: These papers verify claims against retrieved evidence, score the factuality of long-form generations and detect fake news, including robustness to conflicting or adversarial evidence.

88.name: Agent Safety and Tool-Use Risks
88.one_line: These papers benchmark and guard tool-using agents against unsafe actions, prompt injection, malicious skills, privacy leaks and backdoors during multi-step execution.

89.name: Low-Bit Weight and Activation Quantization
89.one_line: These papers compress model weights, activations and KV caches with post-training, mixed-precision, ternary and quantization-aware methods that handle outliers.

90.name: Knowledge Graph Reasoning and Link Prediction
90.one_line: These papers reason over knowledge graphs and text-attributed graphs, covering KGQA, temporal knowledge graph forecasting, link prediction and graph serialization for language models.

91.name: Audio-Language Model Understanding and Reasoning
91.one_line: These papers benchmark and improve large audio-language models on acoustic perception, audio reasoning, bias, over-refusal and audio deepfake detection.

92.name: LoRA and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
92.one_line: These papers improve low-rank adaptation through rank allocation, initialization and multi-task packing, and use adapters to limit forgetting in continual and federated fine-tuning.

93.name: Meme Understanding and Harmful Meme Detection
93.one_line: These papers build multimodal models and multilingual benchmarks to interpret memes, humor and cultural references and to detect hateful or harmful memes.

94.name: Detoxification and Moderation Evasion
94.one_line: These papers reduce toxic generations, generate counterspeech and study how harmful content, fake news and poisoned corpora evade detectors, with a few loosely related robustness papers mixed in.

95.name: Vision-Language-Action and Embodied Agents
95.one_line: These papers build and diagnose vision-language-action policies for robot manipulation, navigation and autonomous driving, including grounding, planning and paraphrase robustness.

96.name: Privacy Leakage, PII and Membership Inference
96.one_line: These papers measure and mitigate privacy risks through PII detection, text sanitization, re-identification audits, membership inference and contextual integrity in agents.

97.name: Financial NLP Benchmarks and Agents
97.one_line: These papers evaluate and build models and agents for finance, covering financial reasoning benchmarks, retrieval, forecasting, trading, compliance and hallucination detection.

98.name: Jailbreak and Backdoor Attacks
98.one_line: These papers design jailbreak and backdoor attacks on language and vision-language models and defend against them with detection probes, guardrails and alignment interventions.

99.name: Tokenization and Subword Vocabularies
99.one_line: These papers analyze and redesign tokenizers, including byte-level, grapheme and morphology-aware subwords, and study their effect on multilingual and low-resource modeling.

0.name: Code, Optimization & Chemistry
0.one_line: These papers use language models and agents to write, test and repair code, solve software engineering tasks, discover algorithms through evolutionary search and design molecules and drugs.

1.name: Vision-Language Models
1.one_line: These papers build, benchmark and diagnose vision-language models for images, charts, documents, video, spatial reasoning and embodied action, with work on hallucination and efficient visual tokens.

2.name: Fine-Tuning & Preference Alignment
2.one_line: These papers adapt pretrained models through preference optimization, domain fine-tuning and low-rank adapters while limiting catastrophic forgetting.

3.name: Factuality, Evaluation & Expert Domains
3.one_line: These papers study calibration, fact-checking, knowledge editing, benchmarks and annotation, and apply language models to legal, financial, scientific and enterprise documents.

4.name: Speech & Audio Models
4.one_line: These papers build and evaluate speech and audio-language models for recognition, synthesis, translation, spoken dialogue and audio reasoning.

5.name: LLM Agents
5.one_line: These papers train and benchmark language agents for tool use, web search, GUI control, long-horizon tasks and multi-agent collaboration, along with skill libraries and agentic reinforcement learning.

6.name: Linguistics, Multilinguality & Translation
6.one_line: These papers compare models with human language processing, study cross-lingual transfer, dialects and tokenization, and improve and evaluate machine translation.

7.name: Social Behavior, Bias & Culture
7.one_line: These papers probe the social, cultural and psychological behavior of language models, covering bias, sycophancy, theory of mind, role-play, personalization, user simulation and LLM judges.

8.name: LLM Safety & Security
8.one_line: These papers attack and defend language models and agents through jailbreaks, prompt injection, backdoors, watermarking, privacy protection and safety alignment.

9.name: Retrieval & Structured Knowledge
9.one_line: These papers improve retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation and reason over knowledge graphs, tables, databases, entities and events, including recommendation systems.

10.name: Long-Term Agent Memory
10.one_line: These papers design and benchmark long-term memory systems that let conversational and personalized agents extract, organize and retrieve past information.

11.name: Reasoning & Reinforcement Learning
11.one_line: These papers improve and analyze model reasoning through reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, efficient chain-of-thought, mathematical problem solving and faithfulness diagnostics.

12.name: Text Generation, Style & Detection
12.one_line: These papers analyze writing style and creativity, detect machine-generated text, generate synthetic training data and produce visual artifacts such as webpages and SVG graphics.

13.name: Sequence Model Architectures
13.one_line: These papers analyze and redesign Transformers, linear attention, state-space models and hybrid architectures, covering positional encoding and attention sinks.

14.name: Medical & Clinical NLP
14.one_line: These papers build and evaluate models for medical question answering, clinical reasoning over health records and radiology report generation.

15.name: Efficient LLMs & Decoding
15.one_line: These papers make language models faster and smaller through pruning, quantization, KV cache compression, mixture-of-experts, speculative decoding and diffusion language models, along with work on unlearning.
